Imagine OS · Release 0.0.1

The computer should write the software with you.

Every app you use was finished before you opened it. Imagine OS is the other arrangement: a real model runs on the device, and the software takes its shape from the person holding it. Private. Immediate. Still yours when the network is gone. The runtime is what you can run today. The shell that imagines is what that runtime is for.

The product

Own the machine. Then own the software.

01

Finished software asks you to adapt.

Menus, icons, and workflows are decided before the machine is opened. You learn the product. It does not learn the way you work. The same interface is shipped to everyone.

02

A rented model asks you to send the work away.

The useful part of the computer now lives in someone else’s cluster. Your prompt, your files, and the shape of your day leave the building so a model can answer.

03

Imagine OS keeps both on the device.

The model runs where you are, and the software is composed for the task in front of you. That is the product. Release 0.0.1 is the local runtime it stands on. The shell is the work in front of us.

Proof

Run a model in this browser.

Press the button and a small open model loads into WebAssembly on this device. Nothing is typed in for you, and the tokens are the model’s. This is SmolLM2 135M Instruct at Q4_K_M, not the 20-billion-parameter target. The first run downloads the weights from Hugging Face. Generation is capped at 64 tokens, and after the weights are in memory it does not call a server.

A Hugging Face example is coming soon.

Architecture

        
How a local run works.

        

          

            boole run takes an alias, such as llama3, or a
            repository and quantization. The alias resolves to a GGUF file that
            fits the memory this machine reports. If that file is not in the
            cache, pull downloads it from Hugging Face and resumes
            if the transfer stops. node-llama-cpp then loads the file, opens a
            context, and samples tokens in-process. Standard output is the
            model text. Diagnostics stay on standard error.

            The prompt comes from an argument, a file, or stdin. It is not uploaded by this code.

            llama.cpp through node-llama-cpp. GPU offload when that build provides it, otherwise the CPU. The default context is 2048 tokens.

    Weights
    
            A GGUF file in the local cache. After it is there, generation does not need the network.

            The demonstration on this page is the same family of runtime, compiled
            to WebAssembly, with one thread and no GPU layers. It is a proof that
            inference can happen in the browser. It is not the command-line release,
            and it is not Imagine OS imagining an interface.
          

        

      

    


    

      

        
Privacy and security

        
What stays here, and what does not.

        

          

            
The command line

            

              The published source has no analytics call. The only network
              code downloads a model file from Hugging Face during
              pull. A prompt is passed to the local session.
              The CLI does not sign or attest the weights. You are trusting
              the repository the alias, or you, selected.
            

          

          

            
This page

            

              The runtime and the page are static. The model file is fetched
              only after you press the button, from one public Hugging Face
              URL. During generation the page counts new network requests and
              reports that count. There is no account and no telemetry pixel.
              This is not a security certification.
            

          

        

      

    


    

      

        
Research roadmap

        
Where the work is going.

        
These are goals. Boole has not published a measurement for them.

        
    
          
  1. 
            Goal
            
    Ternary weights
    
            
    BitNet-style 1.58-bit models, so a full network can live on the device instead of in a cluster.
    
          
    2. 
          
  2. 
            Goal
            
    20 billion parameters, 200 tokens a second
    
            
    A speed target for a model of that size. A number we are aiming at. Not a number we have measured. The speed in the demonstration above is whatever this browser just produced on a 135M model.
    
          
    3. 
          
  3. 
            Goal
            
    A shell that keeps shaping software
    
            
    The default interface is a beginning. The longer work is software that changes with use, with the model still running locally.

For builders

        
Release 0.0.1

        

          
            
Installnpx @boole/cli

            
runPrompt a local model. An alias such as llama3 picks a quantization that fits available memory.

            
pullDownload weights into the cache. An interrupted download resumes.

            
doctorRead the machine and suggest a size it can hold.

            
modelsList the aliases.

            
Not builtserve and list are reserved and not implemented. If node-llama-cpp is missing, the CLI says so and stops.

            
PackageThe command-line runtime is published as @boole/cli.
